ld-twelve-mile-house.st: A logger's memoir of the 1870s tote-road walk from Eau Claire to the pineries describes the trip. The first night was spent at the Twelve Mile House, then kept by Pete Pinkum, brother of John Pinkum of the West Side sawmill (Empire Lumber). The next stops north were the Lake House on lower Long Lake and the Big Bend (Eau Claire Leader, 29 Jun 1917, p. 3).
src: Eau Claire Leader, 29 Jun 1917, p. 3 (newspapers.com image 239482597)

pc88-lake-house-on-long-lake-sec-18-t32n.st: In the 1870s the Lake House on lower Long Lake was the dinner stop on the second day of the tote-road walk from Eau Claire to the pineries, between the Twelve Mile House and the Big Bend. It was later kept by Mr. Campbell, an old Chippewa River steamboat man, who was "still living on the place" in 1917 (Eau Claire Leader, 29 Jun 1917, p. 3). A Frank F. Campbell took a federal patent in 1882 on the NW¼ SE¼ of sec. 12 T32N R9W, about 1.7 km northwest of this pin, which may be the same family.
src: Eau Claire Leader, 29 Jun 1917, p. 3 (newspapers.com image 239482597)
